title: Efficacy and safety of prednisone in the treatment of idiosyncratic hepatotoxicity
official: «Mitochondrial functionality and oxidative stress in a phase II study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of corticosteroid treatment in hepatotoxicity»
summary:
Main objective: To assess if oral prednisone (compared to placebo), administered over five weeks is beneficial in terms of decreased TBL, i.e., reduction of the peak of TBL by at least 50% at 14 days or reduction time to normalisation of TBL value.
To assess if oral prednisone (compared to placebo) is safe and well tolerated in patients with acute moderate to severe DILI.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Female and male patients, aged ≥ 18 years
2. Patients who have been diagnosed with DILI by the expert committee
3. Patients with moderate to severe DILI (elevations of ALT or AST ≥ 5 x ULN and serum TBL ≥ 2.5 mg/dL.
4. Patients who do not show a 15% reduction in ALT values or TBL continues to increase 5-10 days after liver damage recognition despite the withdrawal of the culprit drug.
Exclusion criteria:
1. No clear DILI diagnosis after an expert committee DILI assessment.
2. Inability to provide informed consent
3. Presence of clinically significant comorbid illnesses (by clinician’s criteria) that might impede completion of the study.
4. DILI due to immune-checkpoint inhibitors
5. Presence of active infection as evidenced by positive urine or blood culture.
6. Acute liver failure (INR > 1.5 and hepatic encephalopathy)
7. Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) ≥ 30.
8. Known hypersensitivity to prednisone or placebo components
9. Pregnant or nursing mothers
10. Co-existing infection with hepatitis C, hepatitis B, or HIV
11. Patients already receiving systemic steroids or other immunosuppressants
